ios.desc:
Your calendar, as a stack of paper. Every day in Hibi is a soft, textured page you can doodle on, cover in stickers, and make entirely your own, wrapped around a real calendar that quietly keeps up with your life.

Hibi shows your existing calendars and reminders through Apple's built-in system. No account, no sign-up, nothing to set up. Just three views:

• Day: paper cards you tear away with a swipe
• Week: your days in a gentle stream
• Month: one endless, uncluttered grid

Then it hands you the pens:

• Draw and write by hand, with Apple Pencil support on iPad
• Add stickers, or make your own by cutting them straight from your photos
• Choose your paper, ruling, and colour, and arrange each page the way you like

The details are cared for: hand-picked pastel tints for each of your calendars, live weather on every page from Apple Weather, elegant serif type, a proper dark mode, and home-screen widgets for today's page and what's coming next, unlocked with Hibi Plus.

Private by design. No Hibi account or advertising tracking. Your decorated pages sync through your own iCloud. If you choose to share usage analytics, Hibi sends limited feature-use information to our self-hosted analytics service. Your calendar, reminders, and page content are never included in analytics.

No subscription. The core app is free. An optional one-time Hibi Plus unlock adds those home-screen widgets, alternate app icons, a personal rubber stamp for your pages, and interactive reminders in your widgets, yours for life.

Hibi is Japanese for "days." We made it so you'd want to open yours.

quotes.text:
Hey HN!

Most calendar apps are good at showing what you have planned. They are not very good at capturing what the day was actually like.

So I built Hibi, a customizable digital planner and calendar for iPhone and iPad. Every day has its own paper-like page. You can change the paper, draw on it, add text, stickers, and Washi tape, while keeping the events and reminders already on your device.

I wanted something practical enough to use as my everyday calendar, but personal enough to capture more than appointments. A place to make each day feel like mine and remember it when I look back.

Hibi is free to try on the App Store. I built it as a solo indie project and would love to hear what you think.
